memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'You can bequeath them to your children as inherited property and can make
them slaves for life, but you must not rule over your fellow Israelites
ruthlessly'" - Lev 25:46 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The verse ends by circling back to the same insistent command: do not rule
over your fellow Israelites ruthlessly. Even amid difficult ancient
regulations, God keeps returning to the theme of mercy. He will not let the
subject of ruthlessness go.

Notice how persistent God is on this point. Three times in this section He
warns against harshness (verses 43, 46, and 53). When Scripture repeats
something, it is underlining what our hearts most need to hear. Evidently the
temptation to be ruthless with those in our power is strong, and God knows it.

Dear friend, this repetition is a gift. God understands the human heart. He
knows how quickly power hardens into cruelty, how easily the strong forget
the weak. So He says it again and again: not ruthlessly, not ruthlessly, not
ruthlessly.

The New Testament sounds the same note for the new community. Masters, do not
threaten your servants, since you know that He who is both their Master and
yours is in heaven, and there is no favouritism with Him (Eph 6:9). Be kind
and compassionate to one another (Eph 4:32).

Wherever you have someone in your care, in your employ, or under your roof,
let gentleness be your governing instinct. God is watching, and He has said
it more than once: not ruthlessly.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Why do I think God repeats this warning against ruthlessness so often?
2. Where has power made me harder than I should be?
3. How can gentleness become my governing instinct with those in my care?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, You warn me again and again against ruthlessness because You know my
heart. Soften me, and make gentleness my instinct toward everyone in my care.
Amen.
